title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is the tail of a remark that begins on the previous page; it carries no new formula. Setting: Grothendieck has been solving the 'lacet' (loop-class) equations (48)(49)(56)/(93). The unknowns are pairs (α_0, f) of 2×2 matrices over Ẑ: α_0 with det ±1, f with det 1, subject to α_0 ρ(α_0)^{-1} = ε l_0^ν (f σ_∞(f)^{-1}). These describe how an automorphism u of the profinite extended group Ŝ^+_{0,3} (that is, π_1 of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, extended by S_3) that respects loop classes and commutes with σ_∞ acts on an abelianized, GL(2,Ẑ)-type quotient.

The additive group Ẑ acts on the set of solutions by (α_0, f) ↦ (l_0^n α_0, l_0^n f). This changes only a, b, r, s (by multiples of 2n) and leaves c, d, t, u fixed. Up to the factor 2, this is exactly the indeterminacy of solutions once c, d, t, u are fixed. So what is intrinsically determined by u is:
- the cyclotomic-type multiplier μ ∈ Ẑ*, together with the signs ε_2(μ), ε_3(μ);
- the four quantities c, d, t, u ∈ Ẑ, subject to
  - (96): ε_2(t²+u²) = ε_3(c²+cd+d²) = 1/μ;
  - (97): c ≡ t ≡ 0 and d ≡ u ≡ 1 mod 2.

On this page Grothendieck says he will, for the moment, ignore the natural normalisation of f inside Π̂_{0,3} (the one that would remove the l_0^n ambiguity, glimpsed in §91 (24bis)). His reason: the computation chiefly brings out the crucial role, in all these 'lacetic' computations, of the four quantities c, d, t, u.

In modern terms, t²+u² and c²+cd+d² are the norm forms of the Gaussian and Eisenstein orders Ẑ[i] and Ẑ[ζ_3]. These orders correspond to the order-4 and order-6 (elliptic) torsion of SL(2,Z), i.e. to the 2- and 3-cycle relations. Condition (96) says μ^{-1}, up to sign, is a norm from both orders simultaneously. This is the GL(2,Ẑ)-level shadow of the GT-type relations, serving the construction on the next page (§45): the homomorphism M̃_{0,3} → GL(2,Ẑ)' and the extension Ñ_{1,1} of Γ̃ by SL(2,Z)^.
errors: No mathematical error on this page; it is a methodological remark. The phrase 'ce que met' is presumably 'ce qui met'.

ideas.what: Deliberately set aside the normalisation of f (removing the l_0^n ambiguity) and regard the invariants μ, c, d, t, u as the intrinsic data of a loop-preserving automorphism commuting with σ_∞
ideas.modern_name: Image of GT-type (loop-preserving) automorphisms in GL2(Ẑ) via abelianised/elliptic data; norm conditions from the Gaussian and Eisenstein orders
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (GT, 1990); Ihara; Lochak–Schneps; Nakamura (Π_{1,1} and GL2 actions), 1990s
ideas.where_published: Only in these unpublished 'Longue Marche' sequel notes (cote 140-3), as far as I know

deep.surprise_reason: Short transitional sentence concluding a remark; it only emphasises the role of c, d, t, u, with no new result.
transcription_corrections: The uncertain word after 'la' reads like 'c[or]..ction' followed by 'crucial,'; possibly 'correction' or 'conviction', and the transcription's '[?] condition cruciale' is uncertain.
'ce que met' should probably be read as 'ce qui met'.
The page number at the top looks like '383' (possibly '388', given that the next page is numbered 389).
